metadata.note: The Rochester, Lockport and Niagara Falls Railroad -- the 'Falls Road' -- incorporated December 14 1850 to buy up the bankrupt Lockport and Niagara Falls Railroad and build a through route between its three namesake cities. Its new 75-mile standard-gauge line opened in July 1852, running west from Rochester along the Erie Canal through Brockport, Albion, Medina and Gasport to Lockport, then southwest to Niagara Falls on a shorter, more direct alignment than its predecessor, passing south of Pekin and the Tuscarora Reservation. It lasted barely a year as an independent company: on May 1 1853 it was one of ten railroads consolidated to form the first New York Central Railroad, where it became the Falls Road Branch. At Rochester it met the Rochester and Syracuse Railroad, and the Buffalo and Lockport Railroad (already on this map as nyc_buffalo_lockport.geojson) soon gave Lockport a direct link to Buffalo. Passenger service ended around 1957, but the line never closed: No scheduled passenger train has run since about 1957, so the line is drawn here only up to that year. The corridor itself never closed -- Genesee Valley Transportation's Falls Road Railroad has run FREIGHT over roughly 45 miles from Lockport east to Brockport since October 1996 -- but freight-only operation is not shown on this map (see ../CLAUDE.md). The one passenger survival is drawn: the seasonal tourist excursions the short line hosts for the on-line Medina Railroad Museum between Medina and Lockport.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rochester,_Lockport_and_Niagara_Falls_Railroad (incorporated December 14 1850 to acquire the bankrupt Lockport and Niagara Falls Railroad; new line 75 miles / 121 km opened July 1852; standard gauge 4 ft 8.5 in; a shorter, more direct route than its predecessor, passing south of Pekin and the Tuscarora Reservation; connected at Rochester with the Rochester and Syracuse Railroad; the Buffalo and Lockport Railroad, founded 1852, soon linked Lockport and Buffalo; consolidated with nine other railroads to form the first New York Central Railroad on May 1 1853)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockport_and_Niagara_Falls_Railroad (incorporated 1834, line between Lockport and Niagara Falls completed 1838, 23 miles / 37 km, operated 1834-1850; acquired 1850 by the Rochester, Lockport and Niagara Falls Railroad, which relocated the line further south and abandoned the original route in its entirety)

http://www.rochester-railfan.net/frrr.htm (the Falls Road Railroad takes its name from the Falls Road Branch designation under New York Central ownership; the Falls Road Railroad subsidiary of Genesee Valley Transportation was formed after the transaction was consummated in October 1996; passenger service ended around 1957)

https://www.american-rails.com/frr.html and https://www.trains.com/trn/railroads/profiles/short-lines/falls-road-railroad-profile/ (Falls Road Railroad runs approximately 45 miles from Lockport east to Brockport through the Erie Canal region; freight traffic is agricultural, perishables, petrochemical and plastics; the Falls Road hosts passenger excursions for the on-line Medina Railroad Museum using Genesee Valley locomotives and the museum's rolling stock, on a seasonal schedule between Medina and Lockport -- scenic trains, wine trains, Day Out with Thomas, The Polar Express)
geometry_sources: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap (Overpass), routed leg by leg through Rochester, Spencerport, Brockport, Albion, Medina, Middleport, Gasport, Lockport, Pekin and Niagara Falls over the surviving Falls Road Railroad / CSX Niagara Subdivision trackage. 79.7 mi against a documented 75 mi (+6.3%, terminal trackage at both ends). Every station matched within 1.4 km of the line. Ways named 'Falls Road' were preferred and the parallel CSX Rochester Subdivision, Belt Line, Ontario Branch and West Shore Subdivision penalised, so the route follows the ex-RL&NF corridor rather than the NYC main line. Ten bridged connector gaps, all under 0.5 km (largest 0.47 km); no straight-line legs. Simplified with Douglas-Peucker at 20 m.
metadata.omitted: The predecessor Lockport and Niagara Falls Railroad (1834 charter, opened 1838, 23 miles) is NOT drawn. The RL&NF relocated the route south in 1850 and the original alignment was abandoned in its entirety 176 years ago; nothing identifiable of it survives in OpenStreetMap. The abandoned ways that do exist in that band north of the 1852 line are later NYC-era branches -- the Ontario Branch, Pekin Railroad, Niagara Branch and Lockport Branch -- not the 1838 grade. Rather than invent an alignment, it is left off; the facts are recorded here instead.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates, not timetable figures. Also unsourced: the exact date passenger service ended (sources say only 'around 1957'), whether the 1852 line opened all at once in July 1852 or in stages, timings and named trains over the Falls Road Branch, the present operating status of the line west of Lockport toward Niagara Falls and east of Brockport into Rochester, neither of which the Falls Road Railroad covers; the year the Medina Railroad Museum excursions began (assumed 1996 here, not sourced); and the exact 1838 alignment. NOTE ALSO a date conflict inside this repo: this file follows Wikipedia in dating the first New York Central consolidation to May 1 1853, whereas schenectady_and_troy_railroad.geojson dates the same consolidation to May 17 1853 citing ICC 1930 pp.211-212. Both are recorded; neither has been reconciled.
metadata.mode_vocabulary_note: This repo's mode values are otherwise passenger categories. 'tourist_rail' is used here for the Medina Railroad Museum excursions, because they are seasonal heritage trips rather than scheduled service. A 'freight_rail' value was briefly introduced for the Falls Road Railroad itself, but that feature was REMOVED on 2026-08-24 under the repo's passenger-only rule (see ../CLAUDE.md and CONVENTIONS.md), so no freight_rail feature remains. app.js does not read the mode field; it is metadata only.
metadata.freight_only_audit: 2026-08-24: removed as part of a repo-wide freight-only audit. Removed here: segment 1957-1996 from nyc-falls-road-branch (explicitly 'Freight only after passenger service ended'); whole feature falls-road-railroad (freight short line; carries no scheduled passengers (its excursions remain, as medina-museum-excursions)). REPO RULE: this map shows PASSENGER rail only. Freight-only operation is not represented -- a line's segments must end when its passenger service ends. See CONVENTIONS.md.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
